description: Stuttering sample player: a fast clock restarts one of five loaded samples from a chosen position, so the sample skips and repeats

params.text: Sets how many clock pulses pass between restarts, none up to ten
Attenuates the DIV CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets where in the sample each restart begins, from its start to its end
Attenuates the POS CV, from nothing through to its full range
Picks which of the five loaded samples plays
Attenuates the WAV selection CV, from nothing through to its full range
Shifts the playback speed by a volt per octave, from -2V to 2V, and below the point where the speed reverses the sample plays backwards
When on, the jump to a new position or a new sample is faded rather than cut, which removes the click

inputs.text: A rising edge advances the stutter count, and a restart happens when the count passes the division; with nothing patched here nothing is restarted
Adds to the restart position after its attenuator, 0-10V covering the whole sample
Adds to the clock division after its attenuator, 0-10V covering none to ten
Adds to the sample selection after its attenuator, 0-10V spanning the five samples
Adds to the playback speed, a volt per octave

outputs.text: The sample being played, taken from its left channel
A 10ms 10V trigger each time the sample is restarted

notes: the output stays silent until a WAV file is loaded into at least one of the five slots under Samples in the right-click menu
menu: Samples — the five numbered items under this label each load a WAV file into that slot, and each prints the filename it holds
Retrigger — restarts the sample from its beginning once it has played to its end
Interpolation — Off, or Linear (Better Quality), choosing how the samples between two stored samples are worked out

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.4: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
